Haight-Ashbury is an incredible relic of San Francisco’s past. The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture.

The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. Within the parks you'll find: Museums, botanical gardens, seasonal music festivals, and a tea garden.

Music City Hotel is located in the vibrant Polk Gulch/Lower Nob Hill neighborhood. Immediately to the left when exiting the Hotel is Polk Street, filled with a wide array of incredible food options, shops, as well as unique bars and nightlife. The neighborhood has historical significance as the original center for San Francisco’s LGBT community and more recently has harbored members of the arts community and important music venues such as Kimo’s, Great American Music Hall, The Regency Ballroom, The Masonic Theater, and more.

In the 1960s at the height of the counterculture movement, a music venue in the neighborhood called The Avalon Ballroom played a vital role in hosting influential acts such as Moby Grape, Quicksilver Messenger Service, and the Grateful Dead. Fast forward to today, and the Polk Gulch has maintained its local charm of both new, modern and long-standing businesses that serve both the neighborhood and beyond.

Russian Hill has evolved into a chic residential neighborhood with outstanding views from every corner. Combined with several great cafes, restaurants, antique shops and boutiques, it’s easy to see why any visitor would gladly leave their heart in San Francisco. Cars line up day after day to drive down nearby Lombard Street, the “crookedest” street in the world, and make the slow creep downhill past charming period homes. Polk Street is the main drag in this neighborhood, where you will find trendy bars, cafes and shops populated with locals, but for one of the most charming rides in the city, grab a cable car heading up and down Hyde Street. Aquatic Park and it's small beach are 3 blocks north. The western edge of Fisherman's Wharf and the Buena Vista Cafe, with it's famous Irish Coffees, is two blocks further (east). The view from the rooftop of the apartment includes Aquatic Park, the Golden Gate Bridge and Fisherman's Wharf.

Recommended Dining in Russian Hill- McCormick
host_about: Originally from Canada, I first came to San Francisco to finish my surgical training at UCSF in the late 1990s, when I moved into the walkup townhouse complex that this studio is a part of. My landlord passed away while I lived there, and I loved the area and the apartment so much that I somehow managed to buy the property from his estate and have continued to live there for many years. I now teach surgical residents for UCSF at their campus in Oakland and have a private practice in Union Square, San Francisco. host_about:
AnneKarin was born in Chicago to Henry P. and Elly Glass.  Theirs was an artistic household.  Henry was educated in the Wiener Werkstadt and was one of the founders of the field of Industrial Design in the U.S.  Elly was a member of the Viennese Dressmakers’ Guild.  Both of them taught at the School of the Art Institute of Chicago.  AnneKarin grew up in Northfield IL and graduated from New Trier HS in 1961.  She received her BA in Anthropology from the University of Illinois, Urbana, in 1966 and joined the Peace Corps that same year.  She served as a Volunteer for three years in Ilheus, Bahia, Brazil, where she founded a leather working factory that provided steady work for local shoe makers.  Upon her return she went to Illinois Institute of Technology where she received an MA in Linguistics.
She tolerated the weather in Chicago until 1973 when she moved to San Francisco where Peace Corps friends facilitated her settlement into a new life on the West Coast.  Two months after she arrived she broke her leg in a ski accident and spent 11 months in a cast.  When able to walk again, she pursued a sign painting business which grew into a brokerage for architectural graphics.  From that she moved into print brokering, specializing in 3-D displays.  This enabled her to buy the house she was living in on Potrero Hill in San Francisco.
The recession in 1989 plus the introduction of computer technology into the world of print created a crossroad.  AnneKarin decided to give up the printing business and return to graduate school where she earned a graduate certificate in Educational Therapy.  She specialized in perception/cognition and opened a private practice, helping children and adults with learning disabilities to address the underlying causes of their learning problems.  
During all these years AnneKarin continued to pursue visual art.  Today she works as an artist, focusing on the figure.  When no model is available she enjoys painting still lifes, abstracts, and landscapes.  She has shown her work internationally and in many competitions across the U.S.  She is a member of the Artists’ Guild of San Francisco.
AnneKarin lives with Clebia, whom she met in Ilheus when she was a Peace Corps volunteer. Clebia is a case worker for intellectually challenged adults and a gourmet cook.  Clebia and AnneKarin enjoy travel, walking in the outdoors, fine dining, music, the ballet, who done-its, and old and new friendships.

host_about:
Greetings!

My name is Warren C. Lathe III, I go by Trey (a nickname, means "3" :). I am a career biologist (molecular genetics) though currently, I'm writing, teaching and other things (like Airbnb!). 

My partner in crime since 1996, and legal husband since 2008, is Guy and we have two school-age (middle and high schools) children (the picture here was 8 years ago :D). Guy is an English as a Second Language teacher by training and career, but now manages properties.

We have a long and deep connection to San Francisco. Guy is a Berryessa. The Berryessa's settled San Francisco and the bay in the 1770s coming with the De Anza party in 1776. His GGrandfather was Jose de los Santos Berryessa.  Guy's parents were married and lived in this city during the '40s (while his father fought in the Pacific theater). My own parents moved to the Bay Area in the 80's. Guy and I both moved into this home in 1997. San Francisco had been our dream city for its acceptance, tolerance, family heritage and its beauty. It has been our permanent home since (though my job took us to  Heidelberg Germany for four years ('99-'03) and DC for two ('12-'14).

Other than science and education, I'm a history, gardening, cooking and travel fanatic :). Guy loves traveling and design. Our eldest is all about acting, singing, make-up, friends, family and the indoors. Our younger is all about dance (Jazz, Modern, HipHop), building things, friends and the outdoors.

Between us we speak passable Korean (me), Swedish (Guy), German (both) and a bit of Spanish (Guy).

Looking forward to meeting you!

Take a stroll along the Rainbow Honor Walk, which celebrates the achievements of LGBTQ+ pioneers, or visit the Harvey Milk Plaza, named after the civil rights leader who lived in the neighborhood.

The Castro is also home to some of San Francisco's best restaurants, cafes, and bars.

Haight-Ashbury is an incredible relic of San Francisco’s past. The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture.

It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality.

The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead.

The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. Within the parks you'll find: Museums, botanical gardens, seasonal music festivals, and a tea garden.

neighborhood_overview:
Pacific Heights San Francisco is a truly beautiful and classic SF neighborhood. It embodies the city you see in the movies with historic and colorful Victorians and mansions. It's also a fun district to go shopping in with locally owned shops as well as internationally recognized high-end brands.

Other fun things to do here include climbing the Lyon Street Steps, soaking in the views of the Bay and checking out the outside of the Mrs. Doubtfire house. You can also enjoy its restaurants, bars, and coffee shops.

It is one of the few areas in San Francisco that survived the 1906 earthquake and fire. This is why you can still find old, colorful Victorian homes from the late 1800s. This upscale neighborhood also has gorgeous mansions lining several of its famous streets.

host_about:
Hello there!

Welcome to my home. I'm really happy you are interested in staying with me. Hosting on Airbnb for 5 years has been a truly humbling experience. Everyone is so kind, genuine and unique. And I'm happy to offer a  safe and convenient place for you to stay in the Silicon Valley.

I work for one of the top 10 Fortune 500 companies, as a Marketing Manager. Marketing is my passion and my B.S. degree. I love it!

When I'm not working, I like to unwind in the hot tub, watch movies, walk downtown for some good food and drink, go glamping (camping with amenities), travel, and play throwback board games. Old school board games like Life, Monopoly, Uno, Pictionary, Sorry, Taboo, Parcheesi, Code Names and any game that involves being silly or yelling.

Being on Airbnb means having a love to travel. Here are some of the fabulous places I've experienced; Vietnam farm and city life, Los Cabos and Ensenada Mexico for the food & drink, Jamaica to get away, Brazil for Carnival, and New Orleans for Mardi Gras. I love Disney and would love to go to all of the Disney parks. For now Disneyland in LA and DisneyWorld in Florida are the 2 places I loved so far.

One thing about being a Silicon Valley native is being so close to some of the BEST and unique foods ever! Do you like Kimchi on your chicken tacos? Prefer to have a machine make your burger for you? Do you crave meat on an bun made all of rice? Is the only way you really want to eat sushi is in a 2 handed burrito or like to get dirty with peel and eat seafood out of a bag? Or are you interested in pairing bourbon with your BBQ? Yummmmmm. So many great places to try. Just let me know what you're interested in.

My life motto is: Do what makes you happy!

My wish is for you to enjoy Happy House, and visit with me here!!  Till we meet in San Jose -- travel with joy and adventure!!

Nestled between San Mateo and San Carlos and situated half-way between San Francisco and San Jose, Belmont Hills is a tranquil residential community in the midst of the culturally and technologically rich Bay Area. 

One of the most sought-after places to live in Northern California, Belmont has excellent schools and easy proximity to biking and hiking. With plenty of parks, preserves, pristine beaches, and shopping centers, Belmont provides the perfect mix of suburban and urban life along with outdoor charm.

Haight-Ashbury is an incredible relic of San Francisco’s past. The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture.

It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality.

The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead.

The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. Within the parks you'll find: Museums, botanical gardens, seasonal music festivals, and a tea garden.

name: Rental unit in San Francisco · ★4.91 · 1 bedroom · 1 bed · 1 shared bath
neighborhood_overview: I LOVE my neighborhood.  First of all, Alamo Square Park is just a block+ away.  It is a very historic park and most of you will recognize it for the views surrounding it.  It is a beautiful place to hang out and look at the scenery and includes a popular dog park.  The houses in my neighborhood are so interesting.  Many were built before the big earthquake and are lovely Victorians.  Since then, many other interesting homes of later origin were built.  Divisadero, one of the earliest routes of the Spanish, is now an 'entertainment corridor' according to neighborhood planners.  It is certainly a destination place for young people and affords all of us plenty of grocery stores, coffee shops, restaurants, clubs, cleaners, et al....most of what you need to keep supplied and entertained.
host_about:
I have been a happy resident of San Francisco since 1994, living right here on McAllister St where I arrived after a former life-time married to a fine man, raising a family of three sons.
I came for a visit and decided to stay......San Francisco does that to you.  I spent my early years here touring the city on inline skates, yes, hills and flat....great adventures, great friends, did the Friday Night Skate for years.   My work and rental property take my time and the fact that I now have 5 dear grandchildren living around the country means I travel rather often.  Now I walk everywhere with Muni as a backup.  SF is a great place to walk, you are never at a loss to find interesting places, beautiful buildings and lovely parks, beaches, trails, whatever your heart desires.  Good way to keep healthy, too, with yoga and gardening added for balance.  I have been renting rooms in my place since 1997 when I was able to purchase it.  I have had hundreds of people stay since then, many from other countries.  I have furnished rooms and cater to students, interns, people new to the city, beginning jobs.....a good place to get a start and figure out where you want to stay more permanently.  I try to make it a home away from home for them.  For me it is like having a large, ever changing family.
Because of the changing politics throughout the world, much of which is troubling,  as angry people take over governments and spread upset and anger about, I think it is valuable to have platforms such as Airbnb bringing people together from everywhere.  The chance to meet, talk, share a meal, converse with a group of people from different countries has to be good for our world.  I have a large map of the world in the living room and each guest puts a pin in the country from which they come.  It is thrilling to see the map fill and know that we have had good times with friends from all of those places!

host_about:
I grew up in San Jose (as A child I recall walking with my 3 siblings to school –or the neighborhood community pool during summer - by way of dirt paths meandering through fruit orchards) and watched the Bay Area transform into the Silicon Valley. My Father was an IRS corporate auditor and my Mother a chemist who became the first female on the board of directors for the Santa Clara County Water District, so when we got home from school, we were pretty much on our own to get our homework and chores completed, and the table set before the parents got home from work. We made a meager allowance, so from a young age I couldn't wait to work for a company and receive a real paycheck.

After working my way full-time through school (in my day we didn’t rely on parents or the government to pay for our school and cars) achieving a BS at SJSU, I worked for 5-years at Menlo Park corporate-based Network General Corporation. I was the 75th employee and when I left to launch my own business, there were 5,000 employees and growing. I was a green (it used to define being “naive” and not saving our deteriorating environment) recruit who quickly became a workaholic, with a fierce, decade plus older bipolar boss, often requiring me to work from 6:00am to 9:00pm six days a week. I absorbed a plethora of business acumen during my tenure - the good, the bad, and the ugly. (Boy did these predominantly Stanford grad, baby boomer techies make modern reality shows seem like preschool- as I witnessed in awe affairs, abuse of power, office politics, hidden agendas, revenge - even to the point of violence - and personal vendettas!) Amongst that chaos (movie worthy!), we launched the diagnostic Sniffer network analyzer and provided network training, GURU consulting and CNX certification. 

Our CEO at the time named Harry Saal who I respected, was on the first “internet superhighway” launch committee. (Yes, that is what we first called the World Wide Web). Technology was moving fast. Shortly after I left NGC, they sold to McAfee. I was married in 1993 and created a downtown San Jose graphic design firm MoonCheese Studios, Inc. (was Derksen Design Group prior to incorporating) which ultimately was acquired by Creatus, a backend and application engineering and placement company, while raising two kids now in college (22 & 24). The Creatus CEO made some bad decisions during the dot com bubble burst (right before 911) and closed the business without notice, leaving to India to run a sister division there, leaving many creditors - including us unfortunately! We began freelancing and had a great stint with Thomas Kincade (yes, the painter of light himself) which allowed my husband to travel the nation in private jets while I worked at home with the kids (hmm) and began intensive volunteering at their elementary school serving as VP of Education, art and  science docent, and even literature (Junior Great Books) docent to instruct the students subjects that city budget cuts removed from their school. 

I was also room Mom for both my children’s classes. We later published a glossy, high-end community magazine (doubling as editor and writer) which highlighted local leaders and heroes selflessly improving the neighborhood, while promoting small businesses via advertising and advertorials for 9 years in both 95120 and Los Gatos (distributed collectively to over 18,000 homes with an 80,000 person reach) so I became very well known in the area. I became a board member for the Almaden Valley Business Association (a subset of the the Silicon Valley Chamber of Commerce) and also a member of the Los Gatos Social Club featuring the who is who (such as current and past Mayors and other politicians, philanthropists, business owners, and activists). 

As publisher, it was rewarding to promote charities and feature the passionate founders, while giving many small businesses a marketing boost and coaching them to produce solid advertising campaigns in our publications. 
Then I survived 3 heart-wrenching challenges in a row (at 41 my Father who was my rock and our family glue passed away, at 42 I was diagnosed with stage 3 breast cancer and experienced 3 near fatal events like staph during treatment which included 7 surgeries, chemo, radiation and so on, and lastly an economic downturn doubled with a divorce so I went from owning 3 properties to 1, but I made it work. 

I began hosting one room via AirBNB in 2017 to explore the operation, learn the app, and see if I could create a sustainable B&B business model. Three years in, I became addicted to it and absolutely love running my successful downtown San Jose business as a Superhost. I love the hospitality industry! 

Personal Likes: Besides valuing time children, I enjoy hiking in the woods or to a beach, fine dining, bike riding, puppies, Napa wine tasting, dancing, photography, writing, marketing and promoting, helping others, charity events, world-wide traveling to exotic locations (I traveled constantly for 4 years, becoming an expert in hospitality), learning other cultures, attending concerts, and spending time with close friends, as well as, meeting new ones.

host_about:
I'm a mid-30's Airbnb Host and Traveler with over a decade in the SF Bay Area, ready to help you find a great home for your short or 1+ month stay. I'm also honored to have over 250 great reviews on Airbnb. While we accept shorter reservations, we specialize in providing furnished homes for 1-12 months, and have noticed many of our customers are business travelers and travel nurses. And we know what they want!

Safe homes with amenities and transportation nearby, close to work, good office chair & desk for working at home, easy check-in without coordinating schedules, large WiFi connected TV's with Netflix to relax, personalized recommendations to meet like-minded folks, access to outdoor and fitness areas... and plenty more. As a former employee traveling for work in the finance industry, I realized that staying in hotels for long periods wasn't all it was chalked up to be... and that I could help provide a better experience for other travelers also. 

I've hosted hundreds of guests from around the US and world, and have studios to 2 bedroom apartments around the San Francisco Bay Area and Silicon Valley: 
- Mountain View
- San Jose
- Redwood City
- Oakland (quick commute to San Francisco)
- Richmond

Send me a message and let's see what we can find closest to your work that meets your needs.

I LOVE the San Francisco Bay Area, and I want you to also! I've lived here for over a decade, and there may be no other place in the world that offers the mix of opportunity, great weather, beautiful nature, urban activities, events, concerts, sporting events, and all kinds of great people.

I'll provide you my own local guide of activities, meetups for your personal interests, and do my best to enjoying your time in the Bay, being productive, staying active, and making the most of your time here (or you're welcome to relax.. we're just here when you need us.)

I have personally stayed in over 25 different Airbnb apartments around the US and the world, so I also know a thing or two about what makes a great furnished home and host. And will do my best to provide that to you. 

A little more about me personally: I've lived in California my whole life, and graduated from San Francisco State University, with a major in Economics and minor in Finance. I've lived all over the Bay Area, including most of the homes I host on Airbnb. I used to work for the State of California in bank regulation, before providing furnished homes and great stays to my guests full-time. 

I enjoy learning and sharing with other Airbnb hosts and real estate investors. In my free time, I also enjoy water color painting, karaoke, beaches, traveling, and making people happy :) 

I realize the San Francisco Bay Area gets very busy and can be quite pricey relative to other locations, so please send me a message so I can see what affordable home we can get you, before everything gets booked up. Thank you for your time.

Haight-Ashbury is an incredible relic of San Francisco’s past. The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture.

It is perhaps the most colorful swath of acreage in San Francisco, and remains one of the last-standing neighborhoods to retain an eccentric personality.

The Haight rose to fame during the Counterculture Movement during the Vietnam War era; it became a regular feature in international news headlines and incited a global initiative for social change with special thanks to the 1967 Summer of Love, and a little help from Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead.

The Haight-Ashbury neighborhood is nestled in between three parks: Golden Gate Park, the Panhandle, and Buena Vista Park, making it somewhat of an urban oasis. Within the parks you'll find: Museums, botanical gardens, seasonal music festivals, and a tea garden.

The winter snow kept coming and they eventually ran out of medicine and food. Unfortunately, they had to resort to cannibalism to survive, which the majority did.

He made a fortune selling gold mining equipment when the gold rush came in 1848-49 and bought a huge swath of land. Haight-Ashbury is an incredible relic of San Francisco’s past. The neighborhood, also known as “The Haight” or “Upper Haight”, succinctly personifies the City’s history, aesthetic, and culture.

host_about:
Hi there! I'm new to the Air B&B community and sure wish I had known about this earlier! I've been living in the amazing city of San Francisco for the last 7 years and am lucky enough to call it home - my whole life has been in the Bay area! I'm working as an ICU nurse at a hospital in SF and one of my favorite past times is to travel! I've been to many countries around the world including Spain, France, England, Italy, Portugal, Argentina, Chile, Uruguay, Costa Rice, Guatemala, Mexico, Australia, Canada, UAE, Nepal, India, Sri Lanka, Japan, Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, Vietnam, Puerto Rico and Aruba! I like to think of myself as adventurous and have found my self doing various things in the above mentioned countries from studying abroad, hiking (recently up to Everest Base Camp), working in rural health clinics, visiting family, scuba diving, attending weddings and just plain old backpacking!

Other hobbies include eating - i love food!, photography, dancing, music and having some good old fun in the sun! My family and close friends mean the world to me and I'm fortunate to have most of them in my immediate surroundings! 

As for guests in my place I'd love to have someone who is respectful, clean and responsible. I live in a great building with an equal amount of elderly folks as young adults, who all greet each other in passing! I like to think I keep my apartment clean and tidy, and love to come home to a nice, clean place as well. I'll be B&B-ing my place for when I'm out of town - I'm pretty easy going and am open to you using most items I leave behind as long as they're cared for (blowdryer, hair straighteners, kitchen appliances, TV). If you find yourself making breakfast and short of an egg or need some condiments - please help yourself. I'd appreciate these privileges not being abused though! I've vowed not to move from my apt until I move out of SF - it's that great and it's location can't be beat!

Immediately to the left when exiting the Hotel is Polk Street, filled with a wide array of incredible food options, shops, as well as unique bars and nightlife. The neighborhood has historical significance as the original center for San Francisco’s LGBT community and more recently has harbored members of the arts community and important music venues such as Kimo’s, Great American Music Hall, The Regency Ballroom, The Masonic Theater, and more.

In the 1960s at the height of the counterculture movement, a music venue in the neighborhood called The Avalon Ballroom played a vital role in hosting influential acts such as Moby Grape, Quicksilver Messenger Service, and the Grateful Dead. Fast forward to today, and the Polk Gulch has maintained its local charm of both new, modern and long-standing businesses that serve both the neighborhood and beyond.

We extend an especially warm welcome to international visiting scholars, interns and the families of Stanford University students, faculty and staff. Our well-equipped kitchen is ready for joyful meals, and on special occasions we get together with our guests and have a potluck dinner.

Music is a big part of our lives, and our living room in the Airbnb where we live is our music room hosting a collection of musical instruments from around the world. Mei Lin likes classical music  Bach & Broadway and plays the piano - , Ross likes Jazz: Miles Davis, Thelonius Monk and he plays the clarinet. 

We enjoy walking, biking, swimming, cross country skiing and gardening.

As hosts we are "no fuss" and want you to feel like you are visiting friends who don't mind if you come and go at any time, We are also good for tips on the area - what to see, where to eat. And we're happy to have a conversation with if you feel like it, or just as happy to let you come and go as you please.

Nestled at the base of Bernal Hill and half a block from Precita Park, this part of Bernal Heights is close to Muni, BART, and the Mission. Precita Park Cafe is 100 steps from the apartment, while nearby Harvest Hills Market offers organic delights.

The apartment is walking distance from many restaurants, bars and shopping. We are one block from the Mission, known for its great dining (including the best burritos in the world), cool bars and unique shopping. It's a perfectly flat walk into the Mission from the apartment so no need to worry about hills in that direction.

Walk South and you will end up on Bernal Hill with 360 degree views of the city (from the very top) and a cool hill top swing that has you soaring over rooftops and flying over a magnificent view of downtown. I have lived in Bernal Heights since 1991 and I adore it. It's a really cute neighborhood with lots of great, thoughtful people. 

The apartment is an in-law in my house. It used to be my office until I realized that I really only need a computer to work and the space was going to waste. A friend came in and redesigned the space for me specifically as a vacation rental (I helped!) and he did a beautiful job. 

Hosting happy guests is my number one priority and all the good reviews really make my day. Come and stay!

host_about:
I grew up in San Jose (as A child I recall walking with my 3 siblings to school –or the neighborhood community pool during summer - by way of dirt paths meandering through fruit orchards) and watched the Bay Area transform into the Silicon Valley. My Father was an IRS corporate auditor and my Mother a chemist who became the first female on the board of directors for the Santa Clara County Water District, so when we got home from school, we were pretty much on our own to get our homework and chores completed, and the table set before the parents got home from work. We made a meager allowance, so from a young age I couldn't wait to work for a company and receive a real paycheck.

After working my way full-time through school (in my day we didn’t rely on parents or the government to pay for our school and cars) achieving a BS at SJSU, I worked for 5-years at Menlo Park corporate-based Network General Corporation. I was the 75th employee and when I left to launch my own business, there were 5,000 employees and growing. I was a green (it used to define being “naive” and not saving our deteriorating environment) recruit who quickly became a workaholic, with a fierce, decade plus older bipolar boss, often requiring me to work from 6:00am to 9:00pm six days a week. I absorbed a plethora of business acumen during my tenure - the good, the bad, and the ugly. (Boy did these predominantly Stanford grad, baby boomer techies make modern reality shows seem like preschool- as I witnessed in awe affairs, abuse of power, office politics, hidden agendas, revenge - even to the point of violence - and personal vendettas!) Amongst that chaos (movie worthy!), we launched the diagnostic Sniffer network analyzer and provided network training, GURU consulting and CNX certification. 

Our CEO at the time named Harry Saal who I respected, was on the first “internet superhighway” launch committee. (Yes, that is what we first called the World Wide Web). Technology was moving fast. Shortly after I left NGC, they sold to McAfee. I was married in 1993 and created a downtown San Jose graphic design firm MoonCheese Studios, Inc. (was Derksen Design Group prior to incorporating) which ultimately was acquired by Creatus, a backend and application engineering and placement company, while raising two kids now in college (22 & 24). The Creatus CEO made some bad decisions during the dot com bubble burst (right before 911) and closed the business without notice, leaving to India to run a sister division there, leaving many creditors - including us unfortunately! We began freelancing and had a great stint with Thomas Kincade (yes, the painter of light himself) which allowed my husband to travel the nation in private jets while I worked at home with the kids (hmm) and began intensive volunteering at their elementary school serving as VP of Education, art and  science docent, and even literature (Junior Great Books) docent to instruct the students subjects that city budget cuts removed from their school. 

I was also room Mom for both my children’s classes. We later published a glossy, high-end community magazine (doubling as editor and writer) which highlighted local leaders and heroes selflessly improving the neighborhood, while promoting small businesses via advertising and advertorials for 9 years in both 95120 and Los Gatos (distributed collectively to over 18,000 homes with an 80,000 person reach) so I became very well known in the area. I became a board member for the Almaden Valley Business Association (a subset of the the Silicon Valley Chamber of Commerce) and also a member of the Los Gatos Social Club featuring the who is who (such as current and past Mayors and other politicians, philanthropists, business owners, and activists). 

As publisher, it was rewarding to promote charities and feature the passionate founders, while giving many small businesses a marketing boost and coaching them to produce solid advertising campaigns in our publications. 
Then I survived 3 heart-wrenching challenges in a row (at 41 my Father who was my rock and our family glue passed away, at 42 I was diagnosed with stage 3 breast cancer and experienced 3 near fatal events like staph during treatment which included 7 surgeries, chemo, radiation and so on, and lastly an economic downturn doubled with a divorce so I went from owning 3 properties to 1, but I made it work. 

I began hosting one room via AirBNB in 2017 to explore the operation, learn the app, and see if I could create a sustainable B&B business model. Three years in, I became addicted to it and absolutely love running my successful downtown San Jose business as a Superhost. I love the hospitality industry! 

Personal Likes: Besides valuing time children, I enjoy hiking in the woods or to a beach, fine dining, bike riding, puppies, Napa wine tasting, dancing, photography, writing, marketing and promoting, helping others, charity events, world-wide traveling to exotic locations (I traveled constantly for 4 years, becoming an expert in hospitality), learning other cultures, attending concerts, and spending time with close friends, as well as, meeting new ones.
